content:
HELB Products: Financing Your Education

Education can be expensive, but the Higher Education Loans Board (HELB) provides a smarter way to finance your studies. HELB offers affordable loans and scholarships to empower students pursuing higher education in Kenya. Whether you are heading to a university or a TVET institution, HELB is designed to support your academic journey.

HELB Loans

If you are looking to further your education, applying for a HELB loan allows you to afford your studies while benefiting from low interest rates. The available loan products include:

TVET Loans: Specifically designed for students enrolled in Technical and Vocational Education and Training institutions.

Undergraduate Loans: Tailored for students pursuing degree programs at recognized universities.

Jielimishe Loans: An additional financing option provided by HELB to assist students in meeting their educational costs.

HELB Scholarships

For students seeking financial aid beyond loans, HELB provides information on various scholarship options and sources available for those studying in Kenya. These include:

ABSA Scholarships: Opportunities for eligible students.

Visa Oshwal Aid: Financial support programs for qualifying students.

Post Graduate Scholarship: Dedicated support for students pursuing advanced degrees.

Partner Funds

HELB has established partnerships with several local and international organizations to assist promising but needy students across Kenya. These funds are critical for students who require extra support to continue their studies after secondary school. Current partner funds include:

HELB Afya Elimu Fund
Civil Servants Training Revolving Fund (TRF)
AIC Kijabe Hospital Fund
Tenwek Hospital Fund
Simba Foundation Fund
ST. Kiz

How to Access HELB Services

HELB provides a centralized digital experience for all users. Students, loanees, institutions, employers, and debt collectors can access specific portals directly through the official HELB website. Key self-service features available on the platform include:

Self Serve: Manage your account and personal details.
Compliance Certificate: Access and download your compliance documentation.
Get-In-Touch: Reach out to HELB for support or inquiries.

What Students Should Do Now

If you are planning to apply for funding, visit the official HELB website at https://www.helb.co.ke/products/ to review the specific requirements and application procedures for each product. Because eligibility criteria and application deadlines can vary by program, you should verify all details directly on the official portal rather than relying on third-party information. Ensure your documentation is ready and monitor the student portal regularly for updates regarding your application status.

The Ministry of Education has an official scholarship listing that includes the **Announcement for the Elimu Scholarship Programme – 2026**. This means the programme appears in the Ministry’s current scholarship information and is being treated as an active official item on the Ministry’s A-to-Z scholarship search page. For Kenyan students and families, this is important because it confirms that Elimu remains part of the Ministry’s scholarship communication for 2026.

Elimu Scholarship is a government-linked scholarship programme associated with the Ministry of Education and implemented through the Jomo Kenyatta Foundation. The official materials in the Ministry’s system show that the programme is connected to learners transitioning to senior school in 2026. Students and parents should therefore pay attention to the Ministry’s official updates rather than relying on rumours, social media posts, or unofficial summaries.

## 2. Who Is Affected
The scholarship is relevant to Kenyan learners who are part of the 2026 Elimu Scholarship process and to families seeking support for school progression. The source materials also show that the programme is associated with learners joining senior school in 2026.

The official information visible in the Ministry’s published scholarship materials shows the scholarship is not limited to one institution. The most important fact is that the Elimu Scholarship Programme 2026 is officially listed by the Ministry of Education. That makes it a verified scholarship announcement rather than an informal notice. The official Ministry page is the key source for confirming that the scholarship is current.

The official materials attached to the Elimu Scholarship Programme 2026 also show that the programme is handled through Ministry and Jomo Kenyatta Foundation processes. The scholarship information includes direction for applicants to use Ministry and JKF channels, which confirms that this is a formal government scholarship pathway.

Another important point is that the source materials indicate the scholarship is connected to learners who are moving into senior school in 2026. UNDERGRADUATE LOANS: HELB GUIDELINES

The Higher Education Loans Board (HELB) provides financial support to students pursuing Bachelor’s degrees. This support is intended for students enrolled in Public and Chartered Private Universities within the East African Community. Eligibility covers students placed through the Kenya Universities and Colleges Central Placement Service (KUCCPS) as well as self-sponsored, parallel, and Module II students. Please note that pre-university, certificate, diploma, and postgraduate students are not eligible to apply for this specific loan.

KEY LOAN DETAILS

These loans are interest-bearing, currently set at a rate of 4% per annum, and include an annual ledger fee of Kshs. 1,000. The duration of loan eligibility is tied directly to the length of your academic program. For example, a student enrolled in a four-year degree program is eligible for four years of funding, while a five-year program qualifies for five years of support. 

APPLICATION TYPES

There are two primary categories for loan applications: 
First-time applicants are those applying for the initial year of their degree program. 
Second and subsequent applicants are those returning to the board for their second, third, or fourth year of study, depending on the remaining duration of their course.

HOW TO APPLY

Students are advised to initiate their application at least one month before the academic term begins to ensure sufficient processing time. To apply, you must visit the official HELB student portal at hef.co.ke. Once on the site, click on the register option to create your personal account and follow the on-screen instructions to complete your application. 

IMPORTANT STUDENT ADVISORY

If you are uncertain about specific documentation requirements, deadlines, or further eligibility criteria not explicitly detailed here, you should verify all information directly through the official HELB website at https://www.helb.co.ke/helb-products/helb-loans/undergraduate-loans/. This scholarship is intended for Kenyan postgraduate students pursuing Master’s or PhD programmes in local public or private universities recognized by the Commission for University Education (CUE). It does not apply to undergraduate, diploma, or TVET applicants. The opportunity is therefore focused strictly on postgraduate academic advancement.

Applicants must have a letter of admission into a full-time or part-time postgraduate university programme. These are the core eligibility conditions confirmed in the official page content and should be stated exactly as they appear in the verified record.

content:
1. What the Elimu Scholarship Programme 2026 Is

The Elimu Scholarship Programme 2026 is an official Ministry of Education scholarship announcement implemented through the Jomo Kenyatta Foundation (JKF). It is designed for Kenyan learners who are joining senior school in 2026 and need financial support to continue their education. The programme remains an important national scholarship reference because the official page was updated on 15 September 2026 and continues to reflect an active selection exercise.

This scholarship should be understood as a government-supported opportunity for learners from disadvantaged backgrounds. It is not a general bursary notice or a private award. The Ministry’s official communication makes clear that the scholarship is part of a broader national effort to support transition into senior school under the Competency-Based Education system.

2. Who the Scholarship Is For

The scholarship targets needy and vulnerable learners joining senior school in 2026. The verified official material also states that applicants should have attained academic achievement within “Meeting Expectation” to “Exceeding Expectation” (Achievement Levels 5–8) in the 2025 KJSEA Assessments. This requirement is important because it defines the academic profile expected for most applicants.

The scholarship is also intended for learners from poor and vulnerable backgrounds. The official announcement and supporting verified material identify groups that may fall under this category, including orphans, learners from urban informal settlements, learners whose parents or guardians live with disabilities, learners affected by HIV/AIDS and other chronic illnesses, and learners from extreme poverty. Learners with special needs and disabilities are also included in the programme’s broader target group.

Because this is an official scholarship notice, only the verified eligibility information should be used. No extra conditions should be added beyond what is stated in the Ministry’s material.

3. National Coverage and County Allocation

One of the strongest verified updates is that Elimu Scholarships are being awarded in all 47 counties. This confirms that the programme is national in scope and not restricted to a single region.

The page also contains a specific county-level update for Muranga County. During the scholarship selection exercise in Muranga County, 127 slots are available in total. Of these, 67 are for girls and 60 are for boys, and the allocation covers all nine sub-counties in the county. This is the most clearly verified county-level detail currently available and should be retained in any article update.

Students and families in Muranga County should treat this slot breakdown as official county-specific information. It does not represent the national total, and other counties will have their own allocation and selection arrangements.

4. Application Forms and Access Points

The official information confirms that application forms could be obtained from the nearest Sub-County Education office. Forms could also be downloaded from the Ministry of Education website or the Jomo Kenyatta Foundation website, and applicants could submit them through the approved online system.

This is an important detail for families because it clarifies the official channels and reduces confusion caused by unofficial copies or social media posts. The safest approach is to rely only on the Ministry of Education, JKF, and the official scholarship portal for forms and instructions.

The scholarship notice also provides a support contact route for applicants and guardians who need clarification. The official notice includes JKF and Ministry contact details for questions or grievances regarding the application process.

5. Scholarship Support and Funding

The Elimu Scholarship Programme is a full scholarship. Verified reporting confirms that beneficiaries receive full school fees, a school kit, transport to and from school, pocket money, and structured mentorship throughout the three years they will spend in senior school.

Additional verified coverage has also mentioned uniforms, personal effects, learning materials, and psychosocial support as part of the broader package. The core verified benefits remain full fees, school kit, transport, pocket money, and mentorship, while the wider support package may also include other learner welfare assistance.

This makes the Elimu Scholarship more than a tuition-only award. It is intended to reduce the financial burden on vulnerable families and help learners remain in school and complete the transition into senior secondary education.

6. Important Dates and Deadline Status

The official application deadline was 23 December 2025 at 5:00 pm. That deadline is the verified closing date and remains unchanged in the official material.

The page was later updated on 15 September 2026, but that update did not reopen the application period. It confirms continued official relevance, not a new submission window. As a result, the scholarship should not be treated as open for late applications unless the Ministry publishes a fresh notice.

For readers checking the article now, the key point is simple: the official page remains active as a reference source, but the original deadline has already passed.

7. How Students Should Apply

During the application period, students were expected to obtain forms from the nearest Sub-County Education office, from JKF, or from the official online channels linked by the Ministry. Completed forms were to be submitted according to the instructions on the official notice.

Because the deadline has already passed, the article should not encourage late submission as if it were still possible. Instead, it should direct readers to the official page for any selection updates, county allocation notices, or further guidance issued by the Ministry or JKF.

If a learner is trying to confirm whether they were eligible, selected, or should have applied during the 2026 cycle, the Ministry and JKF channels remain the correct sources to consult.

title: Mauritius – Africa Scholarship Scheme (MASS) 2026: What Kenyan Students Need to Know
summary: The Ministry of Education has published a 2026 call for applications for the Mauritius – Africa Scholarship Scheme (MASS), an international scholarship opportunity for Kenyan students. The scheme is aimed at undergraduate, master’s, and doctoral study in Mauritius, and the official notice says successful candidates may receive support toward tuition fees and living expenses. Interested applicants must obtain the official Standard Application Forms from the Ministry of Education offices at Telposta Towers or download them from the Ministry website, then submit the required documents by the stated deadline. content:
## 1. What This Announcement Is About
The Ministry of Education has issued a 2026 call for applications for the Mauritius – Africa Scholarship Scheme (MASS) 2026. This is an international scholarship opportunity for Kenyan students who want to study in Mauritius. The official notice says the scheme is offered by the Government of the Republic of Mauritius and is intended for study at undergraduate, master’s, and doctoral levels.

For Kenyan university, college, and TVET students who are planning further study abroad, this announcement matters because it is an official government scholarship call and not a general education notice. It provides a structured route for eligible applicants to compete for places in Mauritius for the 2026 academic intake.

## 2. Who Is Affected
This announcement affects Kenyan students who want to apply for an overseas scholarship under the Mauritius – Africa Scholarship Scheme 2026. The official notice states that the scholarship is open to candidates at undergraduate, master’s, and doctoral levels.

The notice also shows that the scheme is relevant to students who can meet the conditions set out in the application call and who are able to submit the required documents to the Ministry of Education in Kenya. Because the scholarship is advertised through the Ministry’s official scholarships listing, Kenyan applicants should treat the Ministry as the main channel for application guidance and submission.

## 3. The Important Information
The official notice states that the Government of the Republic of Mauritius is offering fifteen (15) scholarships to Kenyan students for the 2026 academic intake. The scholarships are tenable in various universities in Mauritius.

The notice also says the scholarship will support successful candidates in meeting their tuition fees and contributing to their living expenses during their studies in Mauritius. That means the award is not simply an admission notice; it is a funded scholarship opportunity with support for study costs and basic living expenses, subject to selection.

The application process has both an online and a physical component. Applicants are required to apply electronically by filling the official application form available on the Mauritius scholarship portal before printing. In addition, they must obtain Standard Application Forms from the Ministry of Education offices at Telposta Towers, 27th Floor, Room 2702, or download them from the Ministry’s website.

The notice further states that completed forms and supporting documents must be sent to the Director – Higher Education, Ministry of Education, P. O. Box 9583 – 00200, Nairobi, or delivered to the Telposta Towers office.

## 4. Eligibility or Requirements
The official notice includes specific conditions for different study levels, but the details shown in the available notice are incomplete in this summary. What is clear is that the scholarship has separate conditions for undergraduate, master’s, and doctoral applicants.

For undergraduate applicants, the notice states the following requirements:
- Minimum KCSE Mean Grade of B (plain)
- Not more than 25 years of age
- Strong grades in major subjects relevant to the preferred programme
- Completed secondary education in the last three (3) years
- Have an original KCSE certificate

The notice also shows that post-secondary applicants must meet additional conditions tied to their level and study background. Because the official PDF contains more detailed criteria for master’s and doctoral applicants, students should read the full notice carefully before applying and confirm that they meet the stated requirements for their specific level.

## 5. Important Dates and Deadlines
The official deadline stated in the notice is 23rd February 2026. The application forms must reach the Ministry not later than that date.

This is the most important date in the announcement. Students should not wait until the last minute, because the process requires both online completion and submission of printed documents. Late applications would likely not be considered if they arrive after the deadline.

## 6. How Students Can Apply or Access the Service
Students should follow these steps:

- Go to the official Mauritius scholarship application portal and complete the online application form.
- Print the completed online form after filling it electronically.
- Obtain the Standard Application Forms from the Ministry of Education offices at Telposta Towers, 27th Floor, Room 2702, or download them from the Ministry’s website.
- Prepare the required supporting documents listed in the notice, including certified photocopies of the birth certificate and ID, certified academic or professional certificates, transcripts, evidence of application for enrolment in a public higher education institution in Mauritius, and other testimonials.
- Submit two completed copies of the online application form together with the required documents to the Director – Higher Education, Ministry of Education, P. O. Box 9583 – 00200, Nairobi, or deliver them to Telposta Towers, 27th Floor, Room 2702.

Students should make sure all copies are complete and certified where required, because incomplete applications may not be processed properly.

## 7. What Students Should Do Now
Students who are interested in this scholarship should act immediately if they have not already done so. The first step is to read the official notice carefully so they understand the level-specific requirements and the documents needed.

They should then confirm whether they meet the academic and age conditions stated in the notice, especially undergraduate applicants who must meet the KCSE and age thresholds. After that, they should begin gathering certified documents, since these often take time to prepare.

Students should also use the official application portal and the Ministry’s official website rather than relying on shared copies or unofficial summaries. Since the notice is hosted on the Ministry of Education scholarships listing, students should treat that page and the official PDF as the authoritative sources.

## 8. Important Things to Remember
The scholarship is an official 2026 government call, so students should rely only on the terms in the notice.

The notice clearly states that the scholarship supports tuition fees and living expenses, but it does not provide every detail in the summary available here, so applicants should verify the full conditions before submitting.

The deadline is fixed, and the application must reach the Ministry by 23rd February 2026.

Applicants should not assume eligibility based on general academic strength alone; they must meet the specific requirements for their level of study and provide all the documents listed in the notice.

## 9. Official Source
Official source: Ministry of Education, Kenya — Mauritius – Africa Scholarship Scheme (MASS) 2026 notice and scholarships listing.
